short: The Constitution's principal architect, who then lost the capital to a British army.
full:
Madison had drafted much of the Constitution and the Bill of Rights before he reached the presidency. In office he was pushed by the War Hawks of the Twelfth Congress into declaring war on Britain in June 1812, over the impressment of American sailors and trade restrictions imposed during the wars against Napoleon.

The war went poorly. Invasions of Canada failed, and in August 1814 a British force burned the Capitol and the White House, forcing Madison to flee into Virginia. The Treaty of Ghent, signed on 24 December 1814, restored the prewar borders and settled none of the stated causes; news of it reached America after Andrew Jackson's victory at New Orleans, which allowed the whole conflict to be read as a triumph. Madison left office having chartered a second national bank and accepted a standing army, Federalist measures his own party had spent twenty years opposing.
